lesson.menu_desc: Fernando visits three buildings for the next phase of the housing pilot and chooses one with Sarah on a video call -- too, too much, too many and enough (It's too far. The kitchen isn't big enough.) -- 35 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 29 -- Choosing the Next Building
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Fernando Varela | Lesson 29 -- Choosing the Next Building
lesson.grammar_point: too / too much / too many / (not) + adjective + enough / enough + noun

vocab.title: Match each word to its meaning
defs: Easy and useful for you, for example close to the places you need
Full of people, with very little free space
With a lot of loud sounds
The bad part of something that is mostly good
With a lot of light from the sun
The person who owns a house or an apartment and rents it to other people
A machine that carries people up and down in a building
Not expensive, so you can pay for it

items.situation: Think of your office at Einstein. Is anything too small, too noisy or too far? Is anything not big enough?
tips: My office is too... / It isn't... enough

items.situation: Is your team big enough for all the work this year? Answer and explain.
tips: Our team is / isn't big enough... We have too many...

items.situation: Sarah asks: Why didn't you choose Building A? Answer.
tips: It's beautiful, but it's too far...

items.situation: A director asks: Do we have enough money for six apartments? Answer.
tips: Not for six. We have enough money for...

items.situation: Describe the traffic in Sao Paulo at eight in the morning.
tips: There is too much traffic... / There are too many cars...

items.situation: Tell me one downside of your neighborhood, and one good thing about it.
tips: The only downside is... But the best thing about it is...

listenings.text: Good morning, Mr. Varela. This is Carlos Andrade, the landlord of Building C. Thank you for your visit on Tuesday. I have good news for you. I have four apartments for you from January, and for a hospital project, I can lower the rent a little: two thousand five hundred reais a month. I know the kitchens aren't big enough for two families, so I can take out one wall in two of the apartments. The elevator is new, and the street is quiet, not noisy at all. And one more thing: there is a supermarket and a pharmacy on the same street, so it's very convenient for the families. Please call me back this week. Thank you.

Hi Fernando, it's Ana, from the housing pilot. I talked to the families about Building C, and they like it a lot. But they have two worries. First, the bus stop near the building is very crowded in the morning, and some patients are too tired to stand for a long time. Maybe we can use the hospital van. Second, the bedrooms are bright, but in the afternoon they are too hot. We need fans, or maybe air conditioning. And one good thing: the families say the street is quiet enough for the children to sleep. So I think it's a good choice. Let's talk tomorrow. Bye!
